title: Alljoined-1.6M
description: Alljoined-1.6M is a large-scale EEG dataset capturing neural responses to rapid serial visual presentation of natural images from the THINGS database, recorded from 20 healthy adults using a consumer-grade 32-channel EMOTIV FLEX2 system across four sessions each. The dataset comprises over 1.6 million visual stimulus trials and was designed to evaluate whether affordable consumer-grade EEG hardware can support deep learning-based brain-computer interface and semantic decoding research, comparable to costly research-grade systems.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with the EMOTIV FLEX2, a 32-channel wireless (Bluetooth 5.2) consumer-grade system with sintered Ag/AgCl gel electrodes in an extended 10-20 montage focused on occipital/visual regions, sampled at 256 Hz. Participants viewed rapid serial visual presentations of images (100 ms on, 100 ms blank) from the THINGS database while performing an oddball detection task (button press upon detecting a Woody character, ~6% of trials). Raw continuous data were stored as EDF files with 32 EEG channels retained after excluding EMOTIV metadata channels; BIDS conversion was performed using MNE-BIDS with validation via round-trip integrity checks.
